summary: Rate-limit rejections return HTTP 500 instead of 429, breaking client backoff and firing false server-error alarms.
code: for i in $(seq 1 125); do curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' -X POST http://localhost:3002/api/v1/chat -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -H 'X-Real-IP: 9.9.9.9' -d '{"query":"x"}'; done
scenario: Sent 125 POSTs from a single fixed X-Real-IP (9.9.9.9). Exactly 120 returned 202, then every subsequent request returned `HTTP/1.1 500 Internal Server Error` with body `{"error":"Rate limit exceeded. Please wait before sending more queries."}` and headers `x-ratelimit-remaining: 0`, `retry-after: 2`. Zero 429s across all runs. Container logs show `level:50 ... res:{statusCode:500}, err:{error:'Rate limit exceeded...'}`. The custom `errorResponseBuilder` returns a bare object with no statusCode, so @fastify/rate-limit v9's thrown payload falls through to Fastify's generic 500 handler instead of emitting 429. Exploitable/harmful because: (a) well-behaved clients and browsers keying on 429 will not back off, (b) monitoring pages ops on a 500 spike (CLAUDE.md alerts on API error rate >1%), and (c) at a security conference a flood of 500s reads as 'the app is crashing' rather than 'you are being throttled'. No stack trace leaks in the body.
suggested_fix: In the @fastify/rate-limit registration, do not rely on errorResponseBuilder alone to set status. Either return an object that preserves the 429 (the plugin sets reply.code(429) before calling the builder in normal use, so verify the builder isn't overriding it) or add an onExceeding/onExceeded that explicitly does `reply.code(429)`, and add a test asserting the 121st request returns 429 not 500.

summary: POST rate limit is fully bypassable by rotating the client-supplied X-Real-IP (or X-Forwarded-For) header when the web-server is reached directly rather than through nginx.
code: for i in $(seq 1 150); do curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' -X POST http://localhost:3002/api/v1/chat -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -H "X-Real-IP: 10.1.$((i/256)).$((i%256))" -d '{"query":"x"}'; done   # variant: same with X-Forwarded-For and NO X-Real-IP
scenario: The keyGenerator buckets on `req.headers['x-real-ip'] || req.ip` and Fastify runs with trustProxy:true (so req.ip = leftmost X-Forwarded-For). Sent 150 POSTs each with a unique X-Real-IP -> 150/150 returned 202 (0 throttled). Repeated with 150 unique X-Forwarded-For values and no X-Real-IP -> again 150/150 returned 202. Every request mints a fresh bucket, so the 120/min cap never triggers. Prod caveat, stated honestly: nginx-ssl.conf overwrites X-Real-IP with $remote_addr on every request, which closes the X-Real-IP vector at the edge, and because the app prefers X-Real-IP it never falls back to the spoofable XFF path behind nginx. So this is exploitable only when the container is reached directly (exactly the :3002 topology tested, and any future direct-exposure / nginx-misconfig / SSRF-to-container scenario). The app itself has zero rate-limit protection independent of the edge.
suggested_fix: Defense in depth: don't trust an arbitrary client header as the sole rate-limit key. If X-Real-IP is only ever legitimately set by the trusted nginx hop, validate it's present AND that the direct peer (remoteAddress) is the known proxy before honoring it; otherwise key on the raw socket remoteAddress. Alternatively bind the app to listen only on the internal network so it cannot be reached without traversing nginx, and add a small unconditional per-socket cap as a backstop.

summary: ql-9's 'capped/SAMPLED' honesty fix was applied only to athena-hunter's total_rows, but the fields the sweep-4 doc literally names ('total_alerts/flows/dns') live in alert-triage — and they are still uncapped len() of LIMIT-bounded queries presented to the LLM and UI as true totals.
code:
"total_alerts": len(enriched_alerts),
"total_flows": len(conn_flows),   # conn_flows fetched with LIMIT 100
"total_dns": len(dns_logs),        # dns_logs fetched with LIMIT 50
# ...no 'capped'/'sampled' flag anywhere; triage_data JSON dumped verbatim into llm_triage user_content
scenario: A busy window has 5,000 conn flows. athena_conn is called with limit=100 -> conn_flows has exactly 100 rows -> total_flows=100 is put into triage_data and returned in data.total_flows. The LLM (told nothing about the cap) states '100 flows' as a complete count, and the UI renders total_flows:100 as fact. This is the identical 'counts of LIMIT-capped result sets presented as true totals' bug ql-9 claimed to fix; ql-9's own test only exercised athena-hunter's total_rows, so this sibling instance in the agent that actually owns the total_alerts/flows/dns names was never touched.
suggested_fix: Mirror ql-9 in alert-triage: track whether any source query returned exactly its LIMIT (e.g. len(suricata_alerts)>=100, len(conn_flows)>=100, len(dns_logs)>=50) and add a 'counts_sampled': true flag + '(at least N, sampled)' labeling into triage_data before it reaches the LLM, and surface it in the returned data block.

summary: athena-hunter _normalize_severity's comment claims it is 'kept identical' to alert-triage._norm_sev, but the two diverge for word-variants and unknown/empty values — the same alert is labeled differently on the live feed vs. triage.
scenario: Sweep-4 ql-8 aligned ONLY the numeric mapping (1->high). The word/unknown paths were never aligned. severity='error' -> athena-hunter 'low' but alert-triage 'high'; severity='informational (default)' -> athena 'low' vs triage 'informational'; severity='' or garbage -> athena 'low' vs triage 'unknown'. So an ET signature with alert_severity='error' shows as 'low' on the /alerts/recent live feed and 'high' in triage — exactly the cross-surface inconsistency the comment swears it prevents. The comment now actively misleads the next editor.
suggested_fix: Either factor both surfaces onto one shared _norm_sev (import from a shared module), or fix the comment to state the two intentionally differ (athena-hunter's Alert shape has no 'unknown'/'error'/'informational (default)' handling). Do not leave the false 'kept identical' claim.

summary: cc-1's kill-switch fails OPEN on EVERY error path, so the emergency feed-freeze is silently defeated by a single transient orchestrator poll failure (timeout, 5xx, momentary DNS/connection blip) for up to one full KILL_POLL_MS window, resuming the broadcast of real Athena alerts during an active kill.
scenario: Operator hits the emergency kill because sensitive alerts are showing on the demo projector. athenaKilled becomes true on the next 15s poll. Then the orchestrator has one slow/aborted response (AbortSignal.timeout at 10s, or a transient 503) — the catch/non-200 branch sets athenaKilled=false, and the trickle timer resumes dequeuing and broadcasting real restricted alerts to every connected client until a later poll re-confirms the kill. The freeze is only as reliable as an unbroken poll stream, and it fails toward leaking rather than toward safe. The direct questions checked out (fail-safe holds on all paths; athenaKilled can never get STUCK true) — this is the honest flip side: it can get un-stuck at the worst moment. Documented as intended in sweep 4, but the emergency security control is not reliable under orchestrator flakiness.
suggested_fix: Distinguish 'confirmed not-killed' (a 200 with athena_hunter=false) from 'could not determine' (timeout/5xx/parse error). On an indeterminate result, RETAIN the last known athenaKilled state (or fail toward frozen once a kill has been observed) rather than unconditionally clearing to false; only a successful 200 should be allowed to lift an active freeze.

summary: ql-7 (unknown severity -> visible 'unknown' bucket, not buried as 'low') and ql-8 (canonical numeric mapping) were extended to athena-hunter only for the 1/2/3 cases. For unparseable/blank/numeric-4+ severities, athena-hunter's feed normalizer still collapses to 'low', diverging from alert-triage._norm_sev which yields 'unknown' — the same event carries different labels across the feed and triage surfaces, and genuinely-unknown alerts stay buried at the bottom of the feed (the exact defect ql-7 set out to kill).
code:
# athena-hunter _normalize_severity:
return {1: "high", 2: "medium", 3: "low"}.get(n, "low")   # 4+/unknown -> low
# ...else fall-throughs also -> "low"
# alert-triage _norm_sev: same 1/2/3, but unrecognized -> "unknown"
scenario: A Suricata alert with alert_severity '4' (or a NULL/garbage severity) arrives on the live feed via /alerts/recent. athena-hunter labels it 'low' (sorts to the bottom, visually deprioritized), while the same row through alert-triage is labeled 'unknown' and kept visible. ql-8's stated goal ('so the same event isn't labeled differently across surfaces') and ql-7's goal ('unknown must not be hidden as low') are both only half-met. Note this is partly forced by the shared Alert TS type only permitting critical|high|medium|low|informational (no 'unknown'), so a full fix needs the type widened or a distinct visible treatment.
suggested_fix: Either widen the Alert.severity union (and feed rendering) to include 'unknown' and map athena-hunter's out-of-range/unparseable cases to it, or explicitly document that the feed intentionally floors unknowns to 'low' and accept the cross-surface divergence. At minimum keep 4+/blank from silently reading as a benign 'low' if the feed drives any prioritization.

summary: The background-hints guard excludes agent_used values 'orchestrator' and 'guardrail' that can never reach this line, leftover from an earlier control flow.
scenario: 'guardrail' is never assigned to agent_used anywhere in the file (the refused/guardrail path sets agent_used='athena-hunter' and returns early at line 807). 'orchestrator' is the initial value but every routed branch reassigns it before this line, and the two early-return paths (refused L807, kill-switch L856) never reach L902. So only 'error' is a live sentinel here. Not a bug, but the dead sentinels imply a code path that no longer exists and will confuse the next editor reasoning about which paths spawn hints.
suggested_fix: Reduce the guard to the reachable sentinel: `if agent_used != "error":` (or add a comment that 'guardrail'/'orchestrator' return earlier).

summary: _ZONE_RE matches the singular 'Tool' (via 'Tools?') as a restricted zone, so a benign query mentioning 'Tool'/'Tools' is silently short-circuited to a cover response, and legit output containing those words gets rewritten to 'internal'.
code:
_ZONE_RE = re.compile(r"\b(Registration|Tools?)\b")
...
if _ZONE_RE.search(query or ""):
    return True   # query_touches_restricted -> serves cover
...
text = _ZONE_RE.sub("internal", text)  # sanitize_output_text
scenario: The restricted zone is 'Tools', but 'Tools?' also matches the singular 'Tool'. An analyst asking 'Which Tool hosts are beaconing?' (capital T) trips query_touches_restricted and gets a fake 'nothing notable' cover answer instead of real data — a silent false positive that hides genuine activity. On output, a real answer mentioning 'Registration desk' or 'the Tool server' is rewritten to 'internal ...'. (Case-sensitive: lowercase 'tools' is NOT matched, which is itself an inconsistency — an attacker probing with lowercase evades the very filter meant to protect the zone.)
suggested_fix: Anchor to the exact zone token(s): use `\b(Registration|Tools)\b` (drop the optional 's') and decide deliberately on case — if the filter is meant to be robust, add re.IGNORECASE; if it's meant to only scrub the literal proper-noun zone name, document that lowercase is intentionally out of scope.

summary: Two comments describing Gemini thinking_budget=-1 contradict each other: llm_client calls -1 'dynamic/minimal', while athena-hunter calls -1 'UNBOUNDED dynamic thinking'. One of them is wrong and will mislead tuning of the clamp.
code:
# llm_client.py:176  Use -1 (dynamic/minimal) instead ...
# athena-hunter/main.py:335  thinking_budget=0 is clamped to -1 (UNBOUNDED dynamic thinking), and thinking tokens share max_output_tokens ...
scenario: athena-hunter's whole rationale for passing an explicit thinking_budget=512 (instead of 0) rests on the belief that -1 = unbounded thinking that could starve the SQL output and truncate mid-literal. llm_client's clamp comment describes -1 as 'dynamic/minimal', i.e. the opposite risk profile. A future editor reading llm_client will conclude 0->-1 is harmless and may 'simplify' athena-hunter back to thinking_budget=0, silently reintroducing the truncation the 512 was chosen to prevent. Only one description of -1 can be correct.
suggested_fix: Verify the actual Gemini semantics of thinkingBudget=-1 and make both comments say the same thing (Gemini docs: -1 = dynamic thinking, model chooses budget up to the model max — closer to athena-hunter's 'can be large' framing than llm_client's 'minimal').
